prompt:
{
  "public_instructions": "You translate natural-language access-control requirements into Cedar policies using the supplied schema. Cedar denies by default. An applicable forbid overrides every permit. Guard optional attributes with has before reading them. Preserve the schema's entity, set, and attribute types. Use only the supplied task information. Do not use tools, files, search, additional model calls, or external feedback. Produce a single final answer as a JSON object with exactly one field, policy, whose value is the complete Cedar policy text. Do not include explanations or Markdown fences.
",
  "harness": {
    "instruction_blocks": [
      "Translate the requirements into a complete Cedar policy set. Distinguish affirmative grants, necessary conditions, explicit prohibitions, exceptions, and statements that qualifying requests must succeed. Preserve each statement's action, principal population, resource population, and conditions. Interpret related statements together rather than treating every sentence as an independent permission.",
      "A statement that access is allowed only when a condition holds establishes a prerequisite, not an independent grant to everyone satisfying it. A restriction covering several roles does not broaden a grant stated for one role. An explicit must-succeed statement establishes a positive permission obligation; default denial cannot fulfill it. Combine that obligation with applicable prerequisites and prohibitions.",
      "Apply an exception only to the restriction it qualifies. Removing a restriction does not independently grant permission or remove unrelated requirements. A specific exception can qualify an earlier general prerequisite. Preserve conjunctions among jointly required conditions and alternatives among independently sufficient permission paths. Keep different actions separate when their eligibility or conditions differ.",
      "Roles may coexist. Compose grants and restrictions for every applicable role without assuming exclusivity. Use conditional permits for bounded grants and forbids where restrictions must override overlapping grants. Every permit needs textual support; every forbid must retain its stated population, conditions, and exceptions. Do not turn one permission path's prerequisites into global restrictions without textual support.",
      "Use the schema to determine names, types, hierarchy, and representations, not to invent authorization conditions. An owner, assignee, manager, membership, or clearance attribute is mandatory only when the requirements make it relevant. Do not add a role prerequisite to a grant for any person meeting its stated conditions. Use entity equality, hierarchy membership, set membership, and scalar comparisons according to their distinct meanings and schema types. Guard optional attributes before reading them."
    ],
    "input_order": [
      "requirements",
      "schema"
    ],
    "checklist": [
      "Every required action and explicitly required successful request has a supported permission path.",
      "No grant extends beyond its stated principal population, resources, action, or conditions.",
      "Necessary conditions constrain the appropriate grants without becoming unsupported grants or global prohibitions.",
      "Exceptions remove only their qualified restrictions and create no independent permission.",
      "Overlapping roles and overriding forbids preserve required permissions and explicit prohibitions.",
      "No schema relationship or unstated role requirement has become an invented prerequisite.",
      "Cedar names, syntax, types, membership operations, and optional attribute guards match the schema."
    ]
  },
  "requirements": "The system manages deployment approvals in a CI/CD pipeline.

The people involved are committers, approvers, release managers, and SREs. One person may hold both the committer and approver roles, or both the approver and release manager roles, at the same time.

The resources are deployments and artifacts. Every deployment records its committer, approver, target environment, change risk, artifact, and status.

Every artifact records who built it, whether it is signed, its build tags, and its status.

Each requester carries a deploy tier.

Each request carries the current time, source IP, and whether the change is an emergency change.

An approver or release manager may approve a deployment.

An approver who committed a deployment must not approve it.

A release manager who committed a deployment must not approve it.

When a deployment's change-risk score crosses the extra-scrutiny threshold, an approver or release manager may approve it only after it has been submitted for review.

When a deployment's change-risk score does not cross the extra-scrutiny threshold, the submitted-for-review requirement does not block approval.

A request by an approver to approve a deployment that does not trip any prohibition above must be able to succeed.",
  "schema": "entity User {
    isCommitter: Bool,
    isApprover: Bool,
    isReleaseManager: Bool,
    isSre: Bool,
    deployTier: String,
};

entity Artifact {
    builtBy: User,
    isSigned: Bool,
    buildTags: Set<String>,
    status: String,
};

entity Deployment {
    committer: User,
    approver: User,
    targetEnvironment: String,
    changeRisk: Long,
    artifact: Artifact,
    status: String,
    submittedForReview: Bool,
};

action approveDeployment appliesTo {
    principal: [User],
    resource: [Deployment],
    context: {
        currentTime: datetime,
        sourceIp: ipaddr,
        emergencyChange: Bool,
        extraScrutinyThreshold: Long,
    },
};
"
}
